title: Study of the genetic, viral and immune response characteristics of a group of patients infected with the AIDS virus treated early and then subjected to suspension of antiretroviral therapy to define biological markers predicting the control of virus replication after pharmacological treatment
official: Study of a novel combination of immunovirologic and genetic parameters in early-treated HIV-1 patients undergone to antiretroviral therapy interruption (ATI) aimed at defining an algorithm predictive of post-treatment control (PCT)
summary:
Main objective: Step 1: Investigate a set of immune-genetic and viroimmunologic biomarkers that
might be useful to individuate PTC
Step 2: Validate the Predictive Algorithms of PTC
conditions: HIV-1 positive subjects treated with effective antiretroviral therapy during the acute phase of HIV-1 infection
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Male or female, aged 18-60 years
2. Confirmed HIV-1 seropositive documented
3. ART commenced during primary HIV infection, as defined by Fiebig stage
4. Plasma HIV-RNA < 50 copies/ml for at least 24 months
5. CD4+ T cell count > 350 cells/mm3 at the last routine follow-up visit
6. No new AIDS-defining diagnosis or progression of HIV-related disease
7. Able to adhere to an effective ART regimen for the duration of the study
8. Willing and able to give written informed consent for participation in the study
Exclusion criteria:
1. Confirmed HIV-2 seropositive
2. Women who are pregnant
3. History of systemic cancer, such as Kaposi’s sarcoma and lymphoma, or other virusassociated malignancies and/or history of AIDS-defining illness according to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention criteria
4. Active or chronic hepatitis B virus infection, with detectable hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis B virus DNA, or both active and chronic hepatitis C virus infection, with detectable virus RNA, and syphilis
5. Only Step 2 Naso-pharyngeal swab positive for SARS-CoV-2
